contentBlocks.body: `System.Threading.Channels` is the modern async producer-consumer queue: producers call `Writer.WriteAsync`, consumers `await foreach (var item in Reader.ReadAllAsync(ct))`, and nothing blocks a thread while waiting. It is the standard way to hand work from an HTTP request to a background worker in the same process.

**Bounded vs unbounded** is the key design decision. An unbounded channel never makes producers wait, so if consumers fall behind, memory grows until the process dies. A bounded channel forces a choice when it is full, through `BoundedChannelFullMode`:

- `Wait`: the writer awaits until there is space. This is **backpressure**, and the right default when every item matters.
- `DropOldest`: evict the oldest buffered item. Good for "latest value wins" data such as telemetry or price ticks.
- `DropNewest`: evict the most recently buffered item to make room.
- `DropWrite`: discard the item being written; the buffer is unchanged.

`Writer.Complete()` marks the end. Later writes fail (`TryWrite` returns false, `WriteAsync` throws `ChannelClosedException`), but readers still receive every buffered item before `ReadAllAsync` finishes. An in-memory channel is lost if the process restarts, so work that must not be lost belongs in a durable queue or an outbox table.
Channels replace `BlockingCollection<T>` in async code. BlockingCollection blocks a thread while it waits; Channels awaits, which keeps the thread pool free for requests.

payload.explanation: Wait makes WriteAsync await until a consumer frees a slot, so producers slow to the consumer's pace. The Drop modes keep producers fast by discarding data.
